history: v1 of this file (commit dfeeef1) was written before the first official development run. v2 (this file) incorporates three amendments made after that run and before any holdout read; see amendments[].

models.description: Training-period mean of the target among eligible players
models.name: league_mean

models.description: Last season's value, uncorrected (a player who missed the season uses the mean of the seasons they played; with no evidence at all, the training mean)
models.name: persistence

models.description: OLS y = a + b*last_season: regression toward the mean
models.name: regressed_persistence

models.description: OLS y = a + b*last_season + c*age + d*age^2: persistence with an age curve
models.name: regressed_persistence_age

models.description: OLS y = a + b*last_season + c*windowed_history + d*age + e*age^2: simple regression with the same history the candidates see
models.name: ols_history

models.description: The production TEI at the cutoff, as shipped (TEI / 2.5, the scale its own validation used)
models.name: incumbent_tei

models.description: OLS y = a + b*TEI: the incumbent's ranking information put on the target's own scale (applies to every target: it asks what the existing Pivot estimate knows about this quantity)
models.name: incumbent_tei_recalibrated

models.description: Prior = age-adjusted league mean; prediction = prior + b * E/(E+k) * (windowed history - prior), where E is the evidence (minutes or attempts) behind the history and k is chosen by leave-one-transition-out error
models.name: eb_shrinkage

models.description: Ridge on the player's own history only: last 3 values, windowed mean, evidence, age curve
models.name: ridge_history

models.description: Ridge on that history plus the incumbent's box-score z-features (does other box-score information improve the forecast of this target?)
models.name: ridge_boxscore

advance_if_all.folds: candidate has lower MAE than the reference in at least 80% of development folds (4 of 5)
advance_if_all.interval_coverage: pooled development coverage of the nominal 80% interval lies in [0.75, 0.85]
advance_if_all.player_ci: player-cluster bootstrap 95% interval of MAE(candidate) - MAE(reference) lies entirely below 0 on the development folds
advance_if_all.practical: MAE is at least 2% lower than the reference's
advance_if_all.season_ci: the 95% t-interval (k-1 d.f.) of the per-fold MAE differences lies entirely below 0
advance_if_all.team_gate: pie and impact_proxy only: the 95% team-season bootstrap interval of R2(candidate) - R2(reference) for prospective roster-known win% is not entirely below 0; if it cannot be computed the check FAILS

amendments.change: added baseline ols_history (OLS on last season, windowed history, age); incumbent_tei_recalibrated now applies to every target
amendments.reason: independent methodology review: the baselines lacked the candidates' own information, so 'beats the best baseline' could mean only 'uses more than last season'
amendments.when: after the first development run, before any holdout read

amendments.change: added season-level (fold) t-interval, a 2% practical-significance floor, and replaced the concurrent, incumbent-referenced team gate with a prospective, reference-baseline gate that fails closed
amendments.reason: review: the gate was silently skipped for pie, compared a forecast with the TEI on a circular target, and the player bootstrap ignores season-to-season dependence

amendments.change: holdout origins hard-coded; ledger mandatory and keyed by target; development decisions loaded and verified from artifacts; leakage audit strengthened (identity/team permutation, row deletion, population and eligibility compared) and run for every development origin of the primary target; sensitivity is evaluation-only
amendments.reason: review: holdout lock was policy not enforcement; audit could not detect survivorship or identity leaks

claims_not_made: that any model measures underlying ability
that results hold for seasons after 2025-26
that any candidate should be promoted
that the incumbent's score measures impact
preregistration.confirm_on_holdout_if: pooled holdout player-cluster interval vs the development-chosen reference lies entirely below 0 and the candidate improves MAE in every holdout fold
disclosures: an engineering smoke test run before the development/holdout split was enforced in code scored all folds, including the holdout, for impact_proxy with the then-registered models. No model, parameter or rule was changed in response to it; but the impact_proxy holdout is NOT pristine and its confirmation is weaker evidence
the incumbent's own stored validation used the 2024-25 -> 2025-26 transition (one of the two holdout folds)
preregistration.folds: rolling origin; >= 2 training transitions; development = origins 2018-19..2022-23; locked holdout = origins 2023-24 and 2024-25 (hard-coded, independent of later ingestion)
preregistration.multiplicity: six targets x three candidates are examined. Only impact_proxy (the incumbent's own documented target) is confirmatory; every other target is exploratory and is reported without correction

population.evaluated: scored players who played >= 500 minutes in the target season (same rows for every model); training uses the same rule
population.scored: players with >= 200 minutes over the last 3 seasons ending at the cutoff (including those who missed the cutoff season)
population.sensitivity: evaluation-only cuts at 250 and 1000 target-season minutes, training unchanged

preregistration.reference_baseline: the baseline with the lowest pooled development MAE for that target
